**Figure Code for "Risk Perception to Coastal Hazards: a global systematic review"** 

Figure 1 was generated using Covidence and Microsoft Powerpoint 

Figure 5 was partially generated using ArcGIS Pro. Code is included to produce the csv files that were exported to ArcGIS. 

```{r Loading Packages and Data}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(maps)
library(viridis)
library(wordcloud)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(patchwork)
library(ggrepel)
library(ggalluvial)
library(UpSetR)

data_raw <- read_csv("CLEAN_RiskPerception_Review_final.csv",
                     show_col_types = FALSE)

data <- data_raw %>%
  # Drop empty trailing columns
  select(where(~ !all(is.na(.)))) %>%
  mutate(Research_Angle = Research_Angle_of_Risk_Perception, Main_drivers = Main_drivers_identified_for_risk_perception) %>% 
  # Standardize text fields
  mutate(across(
    c(Type_of_Hazard, Risk_perception_measurement_type, Broad_Study_Method,
      country, Participant_Type, Keywords, Research_Angle, Level_of_Analysis,
      Level_of_Risk_Perception, Body_of_Water, Journal),
    ~ str_to_lower(str_trim(.))
  )) %>%
  # Normalize comma-separated values (remove extra white space around commas)
  mutate(across(
    c(Type_of_Hazard, Keywords, Participant_Type, Research_Angle,
      Level_of_Analysis, Level_of_Risk_Perception, Risk_perception_measurement_type, Body_of_Water, Journal),
    ~ str_replace_all(., "\\s*,\\s*", ",")
  )) %>%
  mutate(
    country = case_when(
      country %in% c("united states", "usa") ~ "united states of america",
      TRUE ~ str_trim(country)
    ),
    Level_of_Analysis = case_when(
      Level_of_Analysis == "individual" ~ "individuals",
      Level_of_Analysis == "household" ~ "households",
      TRUE ~ Level_of_Analysis
    ),
    Broad_Study_Method = case_when(
      Broad_Study_Method %in% c("mixed methods", "mixed method") ~ "mixed methods",
      TRUE ~ Broad_Study_Method
    ),
    Risk_perception_measurement_type = case_when(
      Risk_perception_measurement_type %in% c("focus groups", "focus group") ~ "focus group",
      Risk_perception_measurement_type %in% c("key informant interviews", "key informant interview") ~ "key informant interviews",
      Risk_perception_measurement_type %in% c("interview", "interviews") ~ "interview",
      TRUE ~ Risk_perception_measurement_type
    ),
    Participant_Type = if_else(Participant_Type == "general population", "g", Participant_Type),
    Year_of_Publication = as.integer(Year_of_Publication),
    Single_or_Multi_Hazard = str_to_upper(Single_or_Multi_Hazard),
    Single_or_Multiple_Locations = case_when(
      str_to_lower(Single_or_Multiple_Locations) %in% c("m", "multiple") ~ "M",
      str_to_lower(Single_or_Multiple_Locations) == "s" ~ "S",
      TRUE ~ Single_or_Multiple_Locations
    ), 
    Research_Angle = case_when( 
      Research_Angle %in% c("assessment of risk perception level", "assessment of risk perception") ~ "assessment of risk perception level",
      TRUE ~ Research_Angle
    ),
    # Standardize hazard types: combine cyclone with hurricane, remove drought and subsidence
    Type_of_Hazard = str_replace_all(Type_of_Hazard, "cyclone", "hurricane"),
    Type_of_Hazard = str_replace_all(Type_of_Hazard, "hurricanes", "hurricane"),
    Type_of_Hazard = str_split(Type_of_Hazard, ","),
    Type_of_Hazard = map_chr(Type_of_Hazard, ~ {
      hazards <- .x[!.x %in% c("drought", "subsidence")]
      paste(hazards, collapse = ",")
    }),
    Type_of_Hazard = if_else(Type_of_Hazard == "", NA_character_, Type_of_Hazard)
  )

# Canonical allowed hazards (for filtered plots)
allowed_hazards <- c(
  "tsunami", "hurricane", "saltwater intrusion", "sea level rise",
  "erosion", "eutrophication", "storm surge", "pollution", "flooding",
  "climate change"
)
```


```{r Helper tools}
# Split comma-separated column to frequency table
freq_split <- function(df, col, sep = ",\\s*") {
  df |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[col]])) |>
    mutate(term = str_split(.data[[col]], sep)) |>
    unnest(term) |>
    mutate(term = str_trim(term)) |>
    filter(term != "", term != "na") |>
    count(term, sort = TRUE)
}

# Split comma-separated column and count terms
count_split <- function(df, col, sep = ",") {
  df %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[col]])) %>%
    mutate(term = str_split(.data[[col]], sep)) %>%
    unnest(term) %>%
    mutate(term = str_trim(term)) %>%
    filter(term != "") %>%
    count(term, sort = TRUE)
}

# ggplot2 theme for all charts
theme_lit <- function(base_size = 11) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) %+replace%
    theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = base_size + 1, hjust = 0),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = base_size - 1, color = "grey40", hjust = 0),
      plot.caption  = element_text(size = base_size - 2, color = "grey55", hjust = 1),
      axis.title    = element_text(size = base_size - 1),
      legend.title  = element_text(face = "bold", size = base_size - 1),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
}
```


```{r Figure 2}
# Create unique study IDs for the duplicate studies
data_unique <- data %>%
  group_by(study_id) %>%
  mutate(study_id_unique = if (n() > 1) {
    paste0(study_id, "_", row_number())
  } else {
    study_id
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

# Split comma-separated hazards into long format
hazard_long <- data_unique %>%
  separate_rows(Type_of_Hazard, sep = ",\\s*") %>%
  mutate(Type_of_Hazard = str_trim(Type_of_Hazard)) %>%
  filter(Type_of_Hazard != "" & !is.na(Type_of_Hazard))

# Check unique values
unique(hazard_long$Type_of_Hazard)

# Convert to binary matrix
hazards_matrix <- hazard_long %>%
  mutate(value = 1) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Type_of_Hazard,
    values_from = value,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  column_to_rownames("study_id_unique")  

# Clean column names
colnames(hazards_matrix) <- gsub("_", " ", colnames(hazards_matrix))

upset(hazards_matrix,
      nsets = 10,
      nintersects = 25,
      order.by = "freq",
      decreasing = TRUE,
      point.size = 3.5,
      line.size = 1.2,
      mainbar.y.label = "Number of Studies",
      sets.x.label = "Studies per Hazard Type",
      text.scale = c(1.6, 1.4, 1.2, 1.2, 1.6, 1.3),
      mb.ratio = c(0.65, 0.35),
      sets.bar.color = "coral3",
      main.bar.color = "gray30",
      matrix.color = "gray30",
      shade.color = "gray90")
```

```{r Figure 3}
# Panel A 
risk_parsed <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Level_of_Risk_Perception)) %>%
  select(study_id = `study_id`, Year_of_Publication, Type_of_Hazard,
         Level_of_Risk_Perception) %>%
  mutate(entry = str_split(Level_of_Risk_Perception, ",")) %>%
  unnest(entry) %>%
  mutate(entry = str_trim(entry)) %>%
  filter(entry != "", entry != "unk") %>%
  mutate(
    parts             = str_split(entry, "_"),
    n_parts           = lengths(parts),
    risk_level        = purrr::map_chr(parts, 1),
    rest              = purrr::map(parts, ~ .x[-1]),
    survey_tok        = purrr::map_chr(rest, ~ {
      hits <- str_subset(.x, "^s\\d+$")
      if (length(hits)) hits[1] else NA_character_
    }),
    hazard_from_entry = purrr::map_chr(rest, ~ {
      h <- str_subset(.x, "^s\\d+$", negate = TRUE)
      if (length(h)) paste(h, collapse = " ") else NA_character_
    }),
    unified_hazard = case_when(
      !is.na(hazard_from_entry) & hazard_from_entry != "" ~ hazard_from_entry,
      !is.na(Type_of_Hazard) & Type_of_Hazard != ""       ~ Type_of_Hazard,
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    risk_level_clean = case_when(
      str_detect(risk_level, "very.?high|veryhigh") ~ "very high",
      str_detect(risk_level, "^high$")              ~ "high",
      str_detect(risk_level, "^mod")                ~ "moderate",
      str_detect(risk_level, "^low$")               ~ "low",
      str_detect(risk_level, "very.?low|verylow")   ~ "very low",
      TRUE                                           ~ risk_level
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(risk_level_clean %in% c("very low", "low", "moderate", "high", "very high")) %>%
  mutate(unified_hazard = str_split(unified_hazard, ",|/")) %>%
  unnest(unified_hazard) %>%
  mutate(
    unified_hazard = str_trim(unified_hazard),
    unified_hazard = str_replace_all(unified_hazard, " ", ""),
    unified_hazard = recode(unified_hazard,
                            "sealevelrise"       = "sea level rise",
                            "flooding"           = "flooding",
                            "floods"             = "flooding",
                            "cyclones"           = "hurricane",
                            "erosion"            = "erosion",
                            "saltwaterintrusion" = "saltwater intrusion",
                            "saltwaterinstrusion" = "saltwater intrusion",
                            "hurricane"          = "hurricane",
                            "tsunami"            = "tsunami",
                            "climatechange"      = "climate change",
                            "stormsurge"         = "storm surge",
                            "stormsurges"       = "storm surge",
                            "pollution"          = "pollution",
                            "eutrophication"     = "eutrophication",
                            "earthquake"         = "earthquake",
                            .default             = unified_hazard
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(unified_hazard), unified_hazard != "") %>%
  filter(unified_hazard != "earthquake")  # EXCLUDE EARTHQUAKES

# Reverse the order so very low is first (left) and very high is last (right)
risk_level_order <- c("very high", "high", "moderate", "low", "very low")
risk_colors <- c(
  "very low"  = "#2c7bb6",
  "low"       = "#abd9e9",
  "moderate"  = "#ffffbf",
  "high"      = "#fdae61",
  "very high" = "#d7191c"
)

risk_by_hazard <- risk_parsed %>%
  count(unified_hazard, risk_level_clean) %>%
  mutate(risk_level_clean = factor(risk_level_clean, levels = risk_level_order))

risk_by_hazard_pct <- risk_by_hazard %>%
  group_by(unified_hazard) %>%
  mutate(total = sum(n), pct = n / total * 100) %>%
  ungroup()

# Stacked bar: absolute counts with numbers at the top
p_risk_stack <- ggplot(risk_by_hazard_pct,
                       aes(x = reorder(unified_hazard, total),
                           y = n,
                           fill = risk_level_clean)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack") +
  geom_text(data = risk_by_hazard_pct %>% 
              group_by(unified_hazard) %>% 
              summarise(total = sum(n)),
            aes(x = unified_hazard, y = total, label = total, fill = NULL),
            hjust = -0.2, 
            size = 3.5,
            fontface = "bold") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = risk_colors, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(
    title    = "Risk Perception Levels by Hazard Type",
    subtitle = "Absolute frequency of each risk category",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Number of Records",
    fill     = "Risk Level"
  ) +
  theme_lit() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  # This ensures the legend displays in the correct order too
 guides(fill = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE))

print(p_risk_stack)

# Panel B 
library(forcats)

# Load the cleaned data
df <- read.csv("risk_perception_by_hazard_country.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Define ordered risk score factor
score_levels <- c("very low", "low", "moderate", "high", "very high")

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    risk_score = tolower(trimws(risk_score)),
    final_hazard = tolower(trimws(final_hazard)),
    country = trimws(country),
    risk_score = factor(risk_score, levels = score_levels, ordered = TRUE)
  )

# Color palette for risk levels (red-yellow-green)
risk_colours <- c(
  "very low"  = "#2c7bb6",
  "low"       = "#abd9e9",
  "moderate"  = "#ffffbf",
  "high"      = "#fdae61",
  "very high" = "#d7191c"
)
# Find countries with enough articles to be worth faceting
countries_to_include <- df %>%
  separate_rows(country, sep = ",") %>%
  mutate(country = trimws(country)) %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(n = n_distinct(study_id), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n >= 2) %>%
  pull(country)

riskperception_countries <- df %>%
  separate_rows(country, sep = ",") %>%
  mutate(country = trimws(country)) %>%
  filter(country %in% countries_to_include) %>%
  mutate(final_hazard = str_to_title(final_hazard)) %>%
  group_by(country, final_hazard, risk_score) %>%
  summarise(n = n_distinct(study_id), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(country, final_hazard) %>%
  mutate(total = sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = fct_reorder(final_hazard, total), fill = risk_score)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack", colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = risk_colours, drop = FALSE,
                    name = "Risk Perception Level") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_pretty()) +
  facet_wrap(~ country, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Risk Perception by Hazard Type, Faceted by Country",
    subtitle = "Countries with ≥ 2 articles shown",
    x = "Number of Articles",
    y = "Hazard Type"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, colour = "grey40"),
    legend.key.size = unit(0.8, "lines"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
    # Remove minor grid lines, keep major vertical ones
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.5)
  )

print(riskperception_countries)
```

```{r Figure 4}
n_drv_na <- sum(is.na(data$Main_drivers) | 
                  tolower(str_trim(data$Main_drivers)) %in% c("unk", "unknown", "na", ""))

# Start from the original data, not from count_split
drv <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Main_drivers), 
         !tolower(str_trim(Main_drivers)) %in% c("unk", "unknown", "na", "")) %>%
  mutate(term = str_split(Main_drivers, ",")) %>%
  unnest(term) %>%
  mutate(term = str_trim(term)) %>%
  # Now split on period for entries like "policy. experience"
  mutate(term = str_split(term, "\\.\\s*")) %>%
  unnest(term) %>%
  mutate(term = str_trim(term)) %>%
  # Remove any empty strings
  filter(term != "") %>%
  # Standardize terms
  mutate(term_clean = case_when(
    tolower(term) %in% c("demographic", "demographics") ~ "demographic",
    tolower(term) %in% c("spatial") ~ "spatial",
    tolower(term) %in% c("experience") ~ "experience", 
    tolower(term) %in% c("policy") ~ "policy",
    tolower(term) %in% c("belief systems", "belief system") ~ "belief system",
    TRUE ~ tolower(term)
  )) %>%
  # Count unique studies per term
  count(term_clean, name = "n") %>%
  rename(term = term_clean)
```

```{r Figure 5}
# CSVs for ArcGIS Pro 
# ----- DATA CLEANING -----------------------------------------------------------
data <- data_raw %>%
  # Drop empty trailing columns
  select(where(~ !all(is.na(.)))) %>%
  # Standardize country names
  mutate(
    country = str_to_lower(str_trim(country)),
    country = case_when(
      country %in% c("united states", "usa") ~ "united states of america",
      country %in% c("uk") ~ "united kingdom",
      TRUE ~ country
    ),
    # Standardize hazard types to lowercase
    Type_of_Hazard = str_to_lower(str_trim(Type_of_Hazard))
  )

# ----- ALL STUDIES (NO FILTER) -------------------------------------------------
all_studies <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(country)) %>%
  select(everything())

# ----- CALCULATE HAZARD FREQUENCIES (ALL COUNTRIES) ----------------------------
all_hazard_freq <- all_studies %>%
  filter(!is.na(Type_of_Hazard)) %>%
  # Split comma-separated hazards
  mutate(hazard_list = str_split(Type_of_Hazard, ",")) %>%
  unnest(hazard_list) %>%
  mutate(hazard_list = str_trim(hazard_list)) %>%
  count(hazard_list, name = "frequency") %>%
  arrange(desc(frequency))

# ----- CALCULATE HAZARD FREQUENCIES BY COUNTRY ---------------------------------
hazard_freq_by_country <- all_studies %>%
  filter(!is.na(Type_of_Hazard), !is.na(country)) %>%
  # Split countries
  mutate(country_list = str_split(country, ",")) %>%
  unnest(country_list) %>%
  mutate(country_list = str_trim(country_list)) %>%
  # Split hazards
  mutate(hazard_list = str_split(Type_of_Hazard, ",")) %>%
  unnest(hazard_list) %>%
  mutate(hazard_list = str_trim(hazard_list)) %>%
  # Count by country and hazard
  count(country_list, hazard_list, name = "frequency") %>%
  arrange(country_list, desc(frequency))

# ----- COUNTRY SUMMARY ---------------------------------------------------------
country_summary <- all_studies %>%
  # Expand multi-country studies
  mutate(country_list = str_split(country, ",")) %>%
  unnest(country_list) %>%
  mutate(country_list = str_trim(country_list)) %>%
  group_by(country_list) %>%
  summarise(
    n_studies = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_studies))

# ----- CREATE ENHANCED DATASET WITH FREQUENCIES --------------------------------
all_studies_with_freq <- all_studies %>%
  mutate(
    # Split hazards
    hazard_list = str_split(Type_of_Hazard, ",")
  ) %>%
  unnest(hazard_list) %>%
  mutate(hazard_list = str_trim(hazard_list)) %>%
  # Join with frequency data
  left_join(all_hazard_freq, by = "hazard_list") %>%
  # Create hazard with frequency label
  mutate(hazard_with_freq = paste0(hazard_list, " (n=", frequency, ")")) %>%
  # Group back to one row per study
  group_by(across(-c(hazard_list, frequency, hazard_with_freq))) %>%
  summarise(
    all_hazards = paste(hazard_list, collapse = ", "),
    hazards_with_frequencies = paste(hazard_with_freq, collapse = "; "),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ----- PRINT SUMMARY -----------------------------------------------------------
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("COASTAL RISK PERCEPTION STUDIES - GLOBAL SUMMARY\n")
cat("========================================\n\n")
cat("Total studies:", nrow(all_studies), "\n")
cat("Total countries represented:", nrow(country_summary), "\n")
cat("Unique hazard types:", nrow(all_hazard_freq), "\n\n")

cat("OVERALL HAZARD TYPE FREQUENCIES:\n")
cat("--------------------------------\n")

# Function to create a bar plot for a specific region
plot_region_countries <- function(region_name, data = country_region_data) {
  
  region_data <- data %>%
    filter(region == region_name) %>%
    arrange(desc(n_studies))
  
  if (nrow(region_data) == 0) {
    message(paste("No data for region:", region_name))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  region_color <- region_colors[[region_name]]
  total        <- sum(region_data$n_studies)
  n_countries  <- nrow(region_data)
  
  # Dynamically adjust plot height via aspect ratio hint (for saving)
  bar_height <- max(4, n_countries * 0.45)
  
  p <- region_data %>%
    mutate(country_label = fct_reorder(country_label, n_studies)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(
      x    = country_label,
      y    = n_studies
    )) +
    geom_col(fill = region_color, alpha = 0.85, width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = n_studies),
      hjust    = -0.2,
      size     = 3.8,
      fontface = "bold",
      color    = "grey30"
    ) +
    coord_flip() +
    scale_y_continuous(
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2)),
      breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 5)
    ) +
    labs(
      title    = paste0(region_name, " — Studies by Country"),
      subtitle = paste0("Total: ", total, " studies | ",
                        n_countries, " countries represented"),
      x        = NULL,
      y        = "Number of Studies"
    ) +
    theme_lit() +
    theme(
      plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14,
                                        color = region_color),
      plot.subtitle      = element_text(size = 10, color = "grey40"),
      axis.text.y        = element_text(size = 11),
      axis.text.x        = element_text(size = 10),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey90", linetype = "dashed"),
      plot.margin        = margin(15, 20, 15, 15)
    )
  
  return(list(plot = p, height = bar_height))
}
```

```{r Figure 6}
count_journals <- function(df, column_name) {
  df %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[column_name]]), .data[[column_name]] != "") %>%
    count(.data[[column_name]], name = "n") %>%
    rename(term = !!column_name) %>%
    arrange(desc(n))
}

# compute_shannon function with variance calculation
compute_shannon <- function(df, period_label) {
  journal_counts <- count_journals(df, "Journal")
  total_pubs     <- sum(journal_counts$n)
  
  if (total_pubs == 0 || nrow(journal_counts) == 0) {
    message(sprintf("No publications found for %s", period_label))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  journal_counts <- journal_counts %>%
    mutate(p = n / total_pubs)
  
  shannon_H <- -sum(journal_counts$p * log(journal_counts$p))
  
  # Calculate variance for Hutcheson's t-test
  sum_p_lnp_sq <- sum(journal_counts$p * (log(journal_counts$p))^2)
  sum_p_lnp <- sum(journal_counts$p * log(journal_counts$p))
  S <- nrow(journal_counts)  # number of species (journals)
  
  var_H <- (sum_p_lnp_sq - sum_p_lnp^2) / total_pubs + (S - 1) / (2 * total_pubs^2)
  
  list(
    period       = period_label,
    shannon_H    = shannon_H,
    var_H        = var_H,
    se_H         = sqrt(var_H),
    n_journals   = nrow(journal_counts),
    total_pubs   = total_pubs,
    journal_data = journal_counts
  )
}

# Get range of years
year_range <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Year_of_Publication)) %>%
  pull(Year_of_Publication) %>%
  range()

years <- seq(year_range[1], year_range[2])

# Calculate Shannon diversity for each year
shannon_yearly <- map_dfr(years, function(yr) {
  data_year <- data %>% filter(Year_of_Publication == yr)
  result <- compute_shannon(data_year, as.character(yr))
  
  if (!is.null(result)) {
    tibble(
      Year = yr,
      Shannon_H = result$shannon_H,
      Variance = result$var_H,
      SE = result$se_H,
      N_Journals = result$n_journals,
      N_Pubs = result$total_pubs
    )
  } else {
    tibble(
      Year = yr,
      Shannon_H = NA_real_,
      Variance = NA_real_,
      SE = NA_real_,
      N_Journals = 0,
      N_Pubs = 0
    )
  }
})

# Remove years with no data
shannon_yearly <- shannon_yearly %>%
  filter(!is.na(Shannon_H), N_Pubs > 0)

# Print summary
cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("SHANNON DIVERSITY INDEX BY YEAR\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
print(shannon_yearly)

# Linear regression to test for trend over time
if (nrow(shannon_yearly) > 2) {
  trend_model <- lm(Shannon_H ~ Year, data = shannon_yearly)
  trend_summary <- summary(trend_model)
  
  cat("\n============================================================\n")
  cat("TREND ANALYSIS: Linear Regression of Shannon H' over Time\n")
  cat("============================================================\n")
  cat(sprintf("Slope (change per year): %.6f\n", coef(trend_model)[2]))
  cat(sprintf("R-squared: %.4f\n", trend_summary$r.squared))
  cat(sprintf("p-value: %.4f\n", trend_summary$coefficients[2, 4]))
  
  if (trend_summary$coefficients[2, 4] < 0.05) {
    if (coef(trend_model)[2] > 0) {
      cat("RESULT: Significant INCREASING trend in journal diversity over time ***\n")
    } else {
      cat("RESULT: Significant DECREASING trend in journal diversity over time ***\n")
    }
  } else {
    cat("RESULT: No significant trend in journal diversity over time (ns)\n")
  }
  cat("============================================================\n\n")
}

# Pairwise Hutcheson's t-tests between consecutive years
hutcheson_pairwise <- map_dfr(1:(nrow(shannon_yearly) - 1), function(i) {
  year1 <- shannon_yearly$Year[i]
  year2 <- shannon_yearly$Year[i + 1]
  
  H1 <- shannon_yearly$Shannon_H[i]
  H2 <- shannon_yearly$Shannon_H[i + 1]
  var_H1 <- shannon_yearly$Variance[i]
  var_H2 <- shannon_yearly$Variance[i + 1]
  n1 <- shannon_yearly$N_Pubs[i]
  n2 <- shannon_yearly$N_Pubs[i + 1]
  
  # Hutcheson's t-statistic
  t_stat <- (H2 - H1) / sqrt(var_H1 + var_H2)
  
  # Degrees of freedom
  df <- (var_H1 + var_H2)^2 / (var_H1^2 / n1 + var_H2^2 / n2)
  
  # Two-tailed p-value
  p_value <- 2 * pt(-abs(t_stat), df = df)
  
  diff_H <- H2 - H1
  
  tibble(
    Year_Comparison = sprintf("%d vs %d", year1, year2),
    Year_Mid = mean(c(year1, year2)),
    Year1 = year1,
    Year2 = year2,
    H_Diff = diff_H,
    t_statistic = t_stat,
    df = df,
    p_value = p_value,
    Significant = p_value < 0.05
  )
})

print(hutcheson_pairwise)

# Count significant changes
n_significant <- sum(hutcheson_pairwise$Significant)
cat(sprintf("\nNumber of significant year-to-year changes: %d out of %d comparisons (%.1f%%)\n",
            n_significant, nrow(hutcheson_pairwise), 
            100 * n_significant / nrow(hutcheson_pairwise)))

# Hutcheson's t-test comparing first half vs second half of time period
midpoint_year <- floor(median(shannon_yearly$Year))
data_early <- data %>% filter(Year_of_Publication < midpoint_year)
data_late <- data %>% filter(Year_of_Publication >= midpoint_year)

result_early <- compute_shannon(data_early, sprintf("Early period (<%d)", as.integer(midpoint_year)))
result_late <- compute_shannon(data_late, sprintf("Late period (>=%d)", as.integer(midpoint_year)))

if (!is.null(result_early) && !is.null(result_late)) {
  
  H1 <- result_early$shannon_H
  H2 <- result_late$shannon_H
  var_H1 <- result_early$var_H
  var_H2 <- result_late$var_H
  
  # Hutcheson's t-statistic
  t_stat <- abs(H1 - H2) / sqrt(var_H1 + var_H2)
  
  # Degrees of freedom
  df <- (var_H1 + var_H2)^2 / (var_H1^2 / result_early$total_pubs + 
                                 var_H2^2 / result_late$total_pubs)
  
  # Two-tailed p-value
  p_value <- 2 * pt(-abs(t_stat), df = df)
  
  diff_H <- H2 - H1
  pct_change <- (diff_H / H1) * 100
  
  if (p_value < 0.001) {
    sig_label <- "***"
  } else if (p_value < 0.01) {
    sig_label <- "**"
  } else if (p_value < 0.05) {
    sig_label <- "*"
  } else {
    sig_label <- "ns"
  }
  
  cat("\n============================================================\n")
  cat("HUTCHESON'S T-TEST: Early vs Late Period\n")
  cat("============================================================\n")
  message(sprintf("H' difference (Late minus Early): %+.4f (%.1f%% change)", diff_H, pct_change))
  message(sprintf("t-statistic: %.4f", t_stat))
  message(sprintf("Degrees of freedom: %.2f", df))
  message(sprintf("p-value: %.4f %s", p_value, sig_label))
  cat("============================================================\n\n")
}

# Visualization: Time series plot with Shannon diversity
```

```{r Extra Calculations}
# Hazard frequency in top 5 countries 
country_hazard_studies <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(country), !is.na(Type_of_Hazard)) %>%
  
  # Expand multi-country entries
  mutate(country_list = str_split(country, ",")) %>%
  unnest(country_list) %>%
  mutate(
    country_list = str_trim(tolower(country_list)),
    country_list = case_when(
      str_detect(country_list, "province of china") ~ "china",
      TRUE                                          ~ country_list
    )
  ) %>%
  
  # Expand multi-hazard entries
  mutate(hazard_list = str_split(Type_of_Hazard, ",")) %>%
  unnest(hazard_list) %>%
  mutate(hazard_list = str_trim(tolower(hazard_list))) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(country_list), country_list != "",
    !is.na(hazard_list),  hazard_list  != "", hazard_list != "na"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    hazard_list = case_when(
      
      # Storm surge
      hazard_list %in% c(
        "storm surge", "storm surges", "storm-surge",
        "stormsurge", "surge"
      )                                             ~ "storm surge",
      
      # Flooding
      hazard_list %in% c(
        "flood", "floods", "flooding",
        "coastal flood", "coastal flooding"
      )                                             ~ "flooding",
      
      # Hurricane
      hazard_list %in% c(
        "hurricane", "hurricanes",
        "tropical storm", "tropical storms"
      )                                             ~ "hurricane",
      
      # Sea level rise
      hazard_list %in% c(
        "sea level rise", "sea-level rise",
        "sea level change", "slr"
      )                                             ~ "sea level rise",
      
      # Erosion
      hazard_list %in% c(
        "erosion", "coastal erosion",
        "shoreline erosion", "beach erosion"
      )                                             ~ "erosion",
      
      # Tsunami
      hazard_list %in% c(
        "tsunami", "tsunamis"
      )                                             ~ "tsunami",
      
      # Cyclone
      hazard_list %in% c(
        "cyclone", "cyclones",
        "tropical cyclone", "tropical cyclones"
      )                                             ~ "cyclone",
      
      # Typhoon
      hazard_list %in% c(
        "typhoon", "typhoons"
      )                                             ~ "typhoon",
      
      # Keep everything else as-is
      TRUE ~ hazard_list
    )
  ) %>%
  distinct(study_id, country_list, hazard_list) %>%
  count(country_list, hazard_list, name = "n_studies")

# Quick check — all unique hazards and their totals after cleaning
cat("\nUnique hazards after cleaning:\n")
country_hazard_studies %>%
  count(hazard_list, wt = n_studies, sort = TRUE) %>%
  print(n = Inf)

top5_countries <- country_hazard_studies %>%
  group_by(country_list) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(n_studies), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(total)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5) %>%
  pull(country_list)

cat("\nTop 5 countries:\n")
print(top5_countries)

top5_hazard_data <- country_hazard_studies %>%
  filter(country_list %in% top5_countries) %>%
  
  group_by(country_list) %>%
  mutate(
    total_country = sum(n_studies),
    pct           = round(100 * n_studies / total_country, 1)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  
  # Title-case country label, ordered largest → smallest for facets
  mutate(
    country_label = str_to_title(country_list),
    country_label = factor(
      country_label,
      levels = str_to_title(top5_countries)
    )
  )

print(top5_hazard_data)

hazard_colors <- c(
  "climate change"      = "#B3B3B3",
  "cyclone"             = "#8DA0CB",
  "drought"             = "#F781BF",
  "erosion"             = "#E41A1C",
  "flooding"            = "#377EB8",
  "hurricane"           = "#4DAF4A",
  "landslide"           = "#999999",
  "pollution"           = "#FFD92F",
  "saltwater intrusion" = "#66C2A5",
  "sea level rise"      = "#984EA3",
  "storm surge"         = "#FF7F00",
  "tsunami"             = "#A65628",
  "typhoon"             = "#E78AC3",
  "wave action"         = "#A6D854"
)

missing_hazards <- setdiff(
  unique(top5_hazard_data$hazard_list),
  names(hazard_colors)
)

if (length(missing_hazards) > 0) {
  message("Adding colors for unlisted hazards: ",
          paste(missing_hazards, collapse = ", "))
  extra_colors <- setNames(
    colorRampPalette(c("#8DD3C7", "#BEBADA", "#FDB462"))(length(missing_hazards)),
    missing_hazards
  )
  hazard_colors <- c(hazard_colors, extra_colors)
}

p_hazard_bars <- ggplot(
  top5_hazard_data,
  aes(
    x    = reorder(hazard_list, n_studies),
    y    = n_studies,
    fill = hazard_list
  )
) +
  
  # Bars
  geom_col(
    width     = 0.7,
    color     = "white",
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  
  # Count + percentage label beyond bar end
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(n_studies, " (", pct, "%)")),
    hjust    = -0.15,
    size     = 3,
    fontface = "bold",
    color    = "grey20"
  ) +
  
  # One panel per country, ordered largest → smallest
  facet_wrap(
    ~ country_label,
    ncol   = 3,
    scales = "free_y"      # each panel shows only its own hazards
  ) +
  
  coord_flip() +
  
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = hazard_colors,
    name   = "Hazard Type",
    labels = function(x) str_to_title(x)
  ) +
  
  # Room for text labels beyond bar
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.30))
  ) +
  
  # Capitalize y-axis hazard labels (after coord_flip)
  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = function(x) str_to_title(x)
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title    = "Hazard Frequency in Top 5 Countries",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Bar length = number of studies per hazard type  |  ",
      "Multi-hazard and multi-country studies counted in each category"
    ),
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Number of Studies"
  ) +
  
  theme_lit() +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 14),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(hjust = 0.5,   size  = 9,  color = "grey40"),
    plot.caption     = element_text(hjust = 0.5,   size  = 7,  color = "grey60"),
    strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size  = 10),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = "grey70"),
    axis.text.y      = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.text.x      = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.title.x     = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey30"),
    legend.position  = "none",        # hazard names already on axis
    panel.spacing    = unit(1.2, "lines"),
    plot.margin      = margin(10, 15, 10, 10)
  )

print(p_hazard_bars)

# Global North and Global South Calculations 
# Define Global North vs Global South classification
global_classification <- tribble(
  ~region,          ~global_category,
  "North America",  "Global North",
  "Europe",         "Global North",
  "Oceania",        "Global North",  # Australia & New Zealand are Global North
  "Asia",           "Mixed",         # Contains both (Japan, S. Korea vs others)
  "South America",  "Global South",
  "Africa",         "Global South",
  "Caribbean",      "Global South",
  "Middle East",    "Mixed",         # Contains both (Gulf states vs others)
  "Other",          "Unknown"
)

# For more precise classification, define specific Global North countries
global_north_countries <- c(
  # North America
  "united states of america", "usa", "canada",
  # Europe (all listed)
  "uk", "united kingdom", "france", "germany", "spain", "italy", "portugal",
  "netherlands", "the netherlands", "belgium", "denmark", "sweden", "norway",
  "finland", "poland", "greece", "ireland", "switzerland", "austria", "iceland",
  # Oceania developed
  "australia", "new zealand",
  # Asia developed
  "japan", "south korea", "singapore", "taiwan",
  # Middle East developed
  "israel", "saudi arabia", "united arab emirates", "qatar", "kuwait", "bahrain"
)

# Classify each country
country_global_classification <- country_studies_with_region %>%
  mutate(
    global_category = case_when(
      tolower(country_list) %in% global_north_countries ~ "Global North",
      region %in% c("South America", "Africa", "Caribbean") ~ "Global South",
      TRUE ~ "Global South"  # Default for remaining countries
    )
  )

# Calculate totals by Global North/South
global_totals <- country_global_classification %>%
  group_by(global_category) %>%
  summarise(
    total_studies = sum(n_studies),
    n_countries = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_studies))

print("=" %>% rep(60) %>% paste(collapse = ""))
print("GLOBAL NORTH vs GLOBAL SOUTH DISTRIBUTION")
print("=" %>% rep(60) %>% paste(collapse = ""))
print(global_totals)

# Calculate percentage
global_totals <- global_totals %>%
  mutate(
    percentage = round(100 * total_studies / sum(total_studies), 1)
  )

print("\nWith percentages:")
print(global_totals)

# Visualization: Pie chart
p_global_pie <- global_totals %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = "", y = total_studies, fill = global_category)) +
  geom_col(width = 1, color = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  coord_polar("y", start = 0) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(global_category, "\n", total_studies, " studies\n(", percentage, "%)")),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    size = 4,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Global North" = "#2171B5", "Global South" = "#FC8D62")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Global Distribution of Coastal Risk Perception Studies",
    subtitle = "Global North vs Global South"
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11, color = "grey40"),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

print(p_global_pie)

# Bar chart alternative
p_global_bar <- global_totals %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(global_category, total_studies), y = total_studies, fill = global_category)) +
  geom_col(alpha = 0.85, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(total_studies, " (", percentage, "%)")), 
            hjust = -0.1, size = 4.5, fontface = "bold") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Global North" = "#2171B5", "Global South" = "#FC8D62")) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    title = "Studies by Global Region Classification",
    subtitle = paste0("Total: ", sum(global_totals$total_studies), " studies across ", 
                      sum(global_totals$n_countries), " countries"),
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of Studies"
  ) +
  theme_lit() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold")
  )

print(p_global_bar)

# Keyword frequency bar chart
kw_freq <- count_split(data, "Keywords") %>%
  slice_head(n = 20)

p_kw <- ggplot(kw_freq, aes(x = reorder(term, n), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#9467BD", alpha = 0.85) +

  labs(
    title    = "Top 20 Keywords by Frequency",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_lit(base_size = 9)

print(p_kw)
```
